notas: Formato historia: Jingle Bells, primera canción tocada en el espacio (Gemini 6A, 16-dic-1965; Guinness World Records 'First song played in space'; Smithsonian guarda la armónica). Publicada en 1857 como 'The One Horse Open Sleigh' por James Lord Pierpont, no escrita para Navidad (Wikipedia, Mental Floss). Fotos NASA de dominio público en public/assets/media/nasa/.

escenas.dice: December, nineteen sixty-five. Two astronauts in orbit radio Mission Control.
They report a strange object, and a pilot in a red suit.
Then they pull out a tiny harmonica and some bells, and play Jingle Bells.
It's the first song ever played in space.
And it wasn't even written for Christmas. It came out in eighteen fifty-seven, as The One Horse Open Sleigh.
Want to play it tonight? Every note has its letter printed inside, so you just find the key.

December 16, 1965. Gemini 6A astronauts Wally Schirra and Tom Stafford report a strange object in orbit, with a pilot in a red suit. Then Schirra plays a small harmonica, Stafford shakes a set of bells, and Jingle Bells becomes the first song played in space (Guinness World Records). The harmonica and bells are now at the Smithsonian. The song itself was published in 1857 by James Lord Pierpont as "The One Horse Open Sleigh", and it wasn't written as a Christmas song.

Our book has Jingle Bells and 19 more carols with the note name printed inside every note, plus an MP3 practice track for each song. The music in this video is that Jingle Bells track. Printable PDF, US Letter or A4. SheetSmithChile on Etsy.
